subject: castle-front-v3
label: Raheem's CourtyardV3 castle, ported to flat side elevation — gatehouse, wall, tower
notes: WHOSE CASTLE THIS IS, AND WHY THE STYLE IS ANCHORED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. Raheem, 2026-08-16: 'I want the castle that was in the courtyard v three. I made them.' Confirmed from git — the deleted CourtyardV3.scene referenced exactly wall-straight-v3, wall-side-v3, tower-corner-v3, tower-battle-v3 and gate-house-v3. Blue slate and deep gold, ornate, medallioned. It is a completely different castle from the honey-gold-over-violet bastion, and every earlier attempt today came back honey-grey because the route in use takes no style reference and the palette was being carried in prose.

SO THE ROUTE CHANGED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS CONFIG. /create-image-pixen accepts NO style image (sprite-lab.mjs says so outright at the call site). /create-1-direction-object DOES — it is what anchored the Ember Jelly to the hero's own register. His art is now the anchor instead of a description of it.

THE STYLE REFERENCE IS CROPPED BELOW THE ROOF ON PURPOSE. castle-tower-battle-v3 is 126x312 and its top ~96 rows are an octagonal platform drawn as a PLAN VIEW — you are looking down onto the tower floor. That is the exact cue being removed, so handing it to the model as the style anchor would be asking for the tilt while telling it not to. The crop is rows 96..312 trimmed to content: 126x216, pure vertical face, carrying the gold banding, the slate, the medallion, the arched door and the arrow slits.

PALETTE, MEASURED ACROSS THE THREE v3 PIECES rather than eyeballed: gold rgb(209,132,62) and rgb(251,189,104) at R-B +147, a deep saturated amber and not the bastion's pale honey; slate blue rgb(12,33,54) and rgb(29,58,76) at R-B -42 to -47; cool neutral stone rgb(143,139,137) and rgb(110,109,108) at R-B ~0. It rides in the prose as a second anchor behind the style image.

VIEW IS 'sidescroller', NOT 'side'. The enum differs per endpoint — character routes take low top-down|high top-down|side, object and tile routes take top-down|sidescroller. Sending the wrong one is silently accepted and produces the wrong angle, which is how this repo has already bought two wrong-angle batches.

FOUR DESCRIPTIONS IN ONE CALL, BECAUSE THE PRICE IS FLAT. The Ember Jelly run returned SIXTEEN frames for $0.12 from one call with four item_descriptions — four takes each, not one. Asking for a single piece would waste three quarters of what is being paid for. So the four are the three pieces the castle actually needs plus a buttressed wall variant, and each comes back with four attempts at the angle.

SIZE CANNOT BE SENT WITH style_images — 422: 'size cannot be set when style_images are provided, the largest style image determines the output size.' So all four return at roughly the style ref's 216px height and get scaled to fit in the Editor. This is not worth fighting; it is recorded so nobody adds an image_size back and wonders why the call fails.

THE PARAPET TRAP, RESTATED FOR THIS CASTLE. castle-wall-straight-v3.png reads as a crenellated band, a flat GREY FIELD, a second crenellated band — the grey field being the walkway floor seen from above. Two rows of battlements with a floor between them is the signature. The word 'parapet' appears nowhere below, and the flat surface is ALSO stated positively, because on the bastion a negative alone was not enough twice running.

THE WALL MUST TILE, AND MUST NOT TILE VERTICALLY. An earlier attempt today asked for 'seamlessly horizontally tileable' and got wallpaper — three stacked bands of battlements filling the frame, no top and no bottom. The fix is to say what must NOT repeat as well as what must: one row of battlements at the very top and nowhere else, plain coursing all the way down to the bottom edge, only the left and right edges matching.

DO NOT MIRROR-TILE THE WALL IN CODE. Masonry coursing is directional; mirroring is what turned a stair into a symmetric arch in castle-walls-v3. If the seam misses, re-crop to the nearest matching course.

FIGURES ARE NOT DRAWN INTO THIS ART. Raheem wants people on the wall; they will be separate LIVE_* sprites placed in Phaser Editor and read chest-up through the merlon gaps. Asking the model for a figure standing on a walkway is asking it to draw the walkway. So the gaps must be wide and tall enough for a head and shoulders, and evenly spaced so placement is a repeat rather than per-instance guesswork. MEASURE the returned gap before commissioning any figure against it.

BIGGEST RISK ON RETURN. The octagonal faceting is still visible in the style reference even with the roof cropped off, so the model is being shown a receding form while being told to draw a flat one. Check take 1 of every description for a visible top face FIRST, before palette or composition — and remember there are four takes each, so a tilted first take is not a failed run.

PALETTE DRIFT IS NOT A REGENERATION. If a piece returns right in shape but off in hue, that is recolor.py against the measured values above. Three generations have already been spent in this repo on colour alone.

OUTPUT SIZE CAPS HOW MANY ITEMS ONE CALL RETURNS, and this is new — the playbook does not have it. Sending four item_descriptions at an effective size of 216 was refused: 422 'item_descriptions has 4 entries but the effective size 216 produces only 1 objects.' The Ember Jelly's sixteen-frames-for-$0.12 was a consequence of its 69px size, not a property of the endpoint. At castle scale it is ONE piece per call, which also means ONE take per piece rather than four — so the gate-one-and-look discipline is not optional here, it is the only safety margin there is.
